transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Wong (Redwood SE), Diego Ramirez (Aurora BI), Priya Shah (Aurora BI), Ethan Cole (Aurora BI)

Summary/Notes (auto-gen - optional):
- Quick recap of last week's tuning (prompt v1 -> v2)
- Reviewed scoring sheet and regression flags
- Action items and owners agreed

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call 
[00:08] Diego: Yeah hi, Diego here. Priya and Ethan are on.
[00:12] Lucas: Morning. We got the updated evals from last week so wanted to walk through top-line.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good, we flagged a couple of items in the sheet where the model regressed on invoice parsing cases.
[00:28] Lucas: Right so high level: prompt v2 reduced hallucinations on product descriptions but introduced some false-positive entity merges on short invoices. We think it's a prompt-context window issue + a KV cache warm-up artifact.
[00:42] Diego: Can you remind me what you mean by KV cache warm-up? I thought that was more runtime stuff on Dedicated?
[00:50] Lucas: Yeah, sorry terminology I mean the key-value attention cache, sometimes when sequence lengths vary the model picks up context from previous tokens when batching. On our hosted runs we saw a small bump.
[01:05] Maya: Note that KV cache note is internal, but it's real; we saw a 1.8% delta in false merges when sequence length < 40 tokens.
[01:15] Priya: We also saw an example where the model changed a payer name to a different company that false positive is concerning for us from a compliance standpoint.
[01:24] Ethan: There's also a throughput question: when you tuned the prompt we've seen latency up ~20% in the 95th. Is that consistent with your numbers?
[01:33] Lucas: Our runs show a modest latency increase on the v2 prompt because it's longer and triggers additional context handling. On Redwood Dedicated or with model quantization we'd expect better tail latency, but for the pilot hosted runs the tradeoff is visible.
[01:47] Diego: Tradeoff cost vs accuracy can you quantify the token cost delta?
[01:53] Maya: Yes, we put numbers in the scoring sheet. Roughly +12% token usage for v2 vs v1 but a 9% improvement on recall for product fields.
[02:03] Priya: For our acceptance criteria we need precision > 98% on payer extraction and no more than 0.5% false merges in a 10k sample. Can you get us there?
[02:15] Lucas: With prompt engineering + a small guardrail classifier we can hit that. Two levers: tighter prompt instructions + post-filter on entities using a lightweight rule-based classifier. We can also add a confidence threshold and surface low-confidence cases to a human-in-loop.
[02:32] Diego: Ok let's talk regression checks. Last week's automated eval flagged 14 regressions out of 1,200 prompts, many were edge cases. Are those reproducible?
[02:40] Lucas: We reproduced about 9 of them deterministically; the rest look intermittent and correlate with batch sizes during load tests. We suspect batching policy and the KV cache behavior I mentioned.
[02:53] Maya: Action: Lucas will run another regression pass where we force batch size to 1 to isolate cache effects.
[02:58] Lucas: Yep will do that and post logs.
[03:02] Priya: Anything on guardrails? We tried a stop-word list but that didn't catch the merges.
[03:10] Lucas: Stop-list isn't enough. We recommend an entity-verification step: after generation, run a small deterministic matcher against your master vendor list. If mismatch, mark for review. That keeps runtime cheap and gives high precision.
[03:24] Ethan: How would that work with our PII redaction flow? We can't send full names to external service in some cases.
[03:31] Maya: For Private deployments we can keep the verification on-prem or in your VPC. For hosted we offer tokenization and partial hashing options; we can share the KMS flow.
[03:43] Diego: Can you also show us an example of the prompt where we got the best recall with acceptable precision?
[03:50] Lucas: Sure I pulled a couple of top-performing prompts into the shared sheet. Example A had defensive instructions and a short structural template; Example B relied on a clarifying question first. Example A traded a little recall for precision which is closer to your goals.
[04:10] Priya: The sheet has the scoring rubric but some of the labels look off (precision/recall columns sometimes blank). Is that a transcribe issue?
[04:17] Maya: That's on us we had manual uploads last night; I'll clean and re-upload the full scoring export.
[04:23] Diego: On the security front, our CISO wanted confirmation on audit logs and SAML SSO timeline.
[04:31] Maya: We have SOC2 in place and can enable SAML SSO; Redwood Private deployments include audit log retention options. I'll attach the security pack to the next email.
[04:44] Priya: Good. About benchmarks can we run a live run on our dev cluster to reproduce the latency/throughput profile?
[04:52] Lucas: Yes we can schedule a live benchmark. We'll need temporary credentials and a sanitized sample of documents. If you give us 1k docs we can run scripted tests and show per-model token latencies and cost estimates.
[05:07] Diego: We'll prep the 1k sample, aim to share by Monday.
[05:12] Maya: Great. Next, questions from Diego: any competitor gaps?
[05:16] Diego: We looked at Anthropic and OpenAI offerings; main differences seem to be model family behavior and enterprise controls.
[05:25] Lucas: Right also deployment flexibility is a differentiator; Redwood supports Dedicated and Private options that help with data residency and audit needs.
[05:33] Priya: One quick clarification: when you say Dedicated, does that mean reserved GPUs we can burst?
[05:38] Maya: Yes, Dedicated = reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and optional burst capacity. We'll share the Dedicated SLA doc.
[05:46] Ethan: Circling back to false merges can you show a couple of failed examples and how the post-filter would catch them?
[05:52] Lucas: I have two examples in the shared folder. Example 1: short invoice where the model concatenated payer+payee because of ambiguous phrasing. Post-filter detects the mismatch against your vendor canonical list and flags for review. Example 2: ambiguous abbreviations we can expand abbreviation mapping as a pre-step.
[06:12] Priya: Useful. For acceptance criteria, if you can get precision >98% and false merges <0.5% we'll sign off on pilot.
[06:20] Maya: Understood. We'll focus on prompt edits + rule-based post-filter.
[06:25] Diego: Timeline when can we expect the regression results?
[06:28] Lucas: I can run the batch-size-1 regression today and post results by Monday 2026-03-30.
[06:34] Maya: I'll send the cleaned scoring sheet and the security docs by Friday 2026-03-27.
[06:40] Diego: And we'll get you the 1k dev sample and the extra prompts by Monday.
[06:45] Maya: Perfect. Any other questions?
[06:48] Priya: None from me.
[06:50] Ethan: All good.
[06:52] Maya: Ok closing notes recap next steps in the sheet, action items assigned. Thanks everyone.
[06:58] Diego: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
notes: Reproduce regressions with batch-size=1 to isolate KV cache effects
Consider adding lightweight entity verifier against canonical vendor list
Share Dedicated SLA and security pack for CISO review
